## Resolution

The owner chose guest autosaves plus optional account sync, same-match Undo that removes the discarded continuation from model context, timed matches with model clock awareness, and a clock that keeps running regardless of leaving the page. The remaining routine defaults below use the owner's standing delegation. This is a product specification, not a claim that a website, chess library, clock service, or live model has been tested.

### Starting a match

Support orthodox chess. Before Start game, the human chooses White, Black, or Random, an advertised model under [Choose the model catalog and opponent selection rules](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-9/choose-the-model-catalog-and-opponent-selection-rules), and a time control. Default to White and 15 minutes per side plus a 10-second increment. Starting minutes must be positive; increment may be zero. Let the player change these settings before starting. MVP games are timed.

Complete connection setup and the required model compatibility check before starting either clock or creating an active game. A failed check leaves setup open. Never spend a player's clock on a pre-game diagnostic.

A normal game starts from the normal position with White to move. A custom-position game follows [Define custom starting positions and position editor](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-19/define-custom-starting-positions-and-position-editor), including its FEN settings, counters, fresh model context, and separate result. The declared side to move determines which clock starts. Do not request a move from an already terminal position.

Start game fixes the initial position, colors, and time control for that game and starts the side-to-move clock. If that side is the model, begin one move request. Changing those setup settings later creates a new game rather than silently rewriting the active one.

### Turns and chess rules

Only the side to move can play. Human illegal board input is rejected without changing the position or stopping the clock; the model's four-illegal-attempt rule does not apply to human input. Human promotion requires a choice of queen, rook, bishop, or knight. The clock runs while that choice is open.

Support king safety, castling, en passant, and promotion, including underpromotion. The application applies only validated moves and checks for an ending after each accepted move. The model remains responsible for choosing its own moves under [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

The casual-play default is automatic draws for stalemate, a dead position where neither side can ever checkmate by a legal sequence, threefold repetition, or 100 half-moves without a pawn move or capture. The threefold and fifty-move thresholds are applied automatically for either side rather than requiring a human claim or a new model draw-claim command. This is a deliberate simplification of claim procedures. Checkmate on the just-accepted move takes precedence over a move-count draw. The architecture ticket must verify actual library support and expose gaps instead of treating a coarse material check as proof of all dead positions. Negotiated draw offers are outside this MVP lifecycle.

Custom starts keep imported half-move counters and begin repetition history at the custom start. A terminal imported setup remains editable, with Start game disabled and an explanation. Do not invent earlier repetition history or normalize counters to make the position playable.

### Clocks run continuously

Only the side to move's clock runs. The other side's clock is stopped until a legal accepted move transfers the turn. Add the configured increment once after a legal accepted move. Rejected, partial, duplicated, canceled, or stale moves earn no increment.

The owner's latest choice supersedes the earlier proposed technical-error clock pause. While a game is unfinished, its active clock keeps running through thinking, streaming, illegal-move and formatting corrections, network/provider errors, rate limits, waiting for Retry, capacity problems, model-switch checks, Stop request, Undo, page navigation, tab closure, browser/device suspension, sign-in, and cross-device handoff. There is no Pause game action. Only an accepted move transfers the running clock; a final result stops it.

A generation interruption leaves the board waiting for recovery, but the chess clock remains live. An HTTP/provider timeout, quota error, or incomplete reply is not itself a resignation, illegal attempt, or immediate loss. The side can nevertheless lose later because its chess clock reaches zero before an accepted legal move. Retry and model switching neither reset nor refill it. Respect retry-after without freezing the clock. A queued model switch still lets the old response finish, except that clock expiry or an explicit Stop/Undo can make that response ineligible.

When the active clock expires, settle one time result and stop actionable generation. The expired side loses on time unless the opponent cannot possibly checkmate from that position through any legal sequence, in which case the result is a draw. The rules dependency must support this position-sensitive distinction; a generic total-material heuristic is not sufficient evidence. A late completed move or early partial move cannot reverse an expired result. The controller must serialize accepted moves, endings, clock expiry, and Undo against one authoritative event order and resolve boundary cases exactly once.

Store remaining time and an elapsed-time reference/deadline, not only the last displayed numbers. Reconstruct elapsed time while a page/device is absent; a suspended JavaScript timer must not freeze the game. On reopening or another device's takeover, reconcile clock expiry before enabling a move, Retry, Undo, or a new model request. If it expired during the absence, record the result at that expiry rather than giving fresh time at reopening.

Clock continuity does not promise that browser-side model generation continues after a tab closes. Only a response actually accepted by the authoritative controller can transfer the turn. An abandoned browser request does not become a move retrospectively. The architecture must verify the chosen timing authority, closed-tab behavior, device sleep, time-source changes, and cross-device ordering without silently moving proxy credentials or generation onto the website's server.

### Model awareness of time

Every move-generation request, including correction requests and manual retries, includes a fresh authoritative snapshot taken just before dispatch. State the model's color, its remaining time in clear units, the human side's remaining time, the selected time control and increment, and which clock is running. Supply this alongside the canonical current FEN and readable piece list.

Label older clock readings in the retained conversation as historical. Instruct the model to finish its independently chosen move within its current remaining time. Do not send a legal-move list or change the independent-move contract to make it faster.

The model sees the snapshot at request time. It does not receive continuous clock updates during one response. Every later request gets a new snapshot. Do not send timer-tick prompts, parallel turn requests, hidden context resets, or provider-native conversation continuations to simulate live clock updates. Prompting the model about time does not guarantee that it responds before expiry.

### Undo in the same match

The owner approved Undo within the existing match and requested that the model forget the undone move. The routine default is one full human decision: return to the previous human turn, taking back the human move and any model reply after it. If a model request is still pending, abandon it before restoring the checkpoint. Repeated Undo can reach earlier human decision points, but not before the game's start or across a fresh-context practice boundary. Before the human has had any decision point, Undo is unavailable.

Restore the checkpoint's position, side to move, castling/en passant rights, move counters, known repetition history, turn recovery budgets, and opponent selection. Discard queued selection changes in the undone continuation. This is an explicit board/history takeback, not a separate Reset retries action.

Restore the corresponding retained match conversation as well. Exclude undone moves, replies, plans/reasoning, corrections, later diagnostics, and any later message revealing that continuation from future model requests. Do not tell the model what was undone or append a summary of it. Use stateless requests constructed from the retained history rather than a provider continuation identifier that could retain discarded turns. Ordinary model switches after Undo carry the complete retained line.

Keep discarded received records in a separate attributed match archive, outside future model context. This preserves the lossless received-data requirement while making Undo an explicit exception to replaying every previously received message. The app cannot erase records already held by the proxy/provider or guarantee deletion from their systems.

Undo does not refund elapsed clock time or restore the old clock readings. Charge the previously active side up to the accepted Undo event, remove increment credits earned only by the undone moves, and start the restored side-to-move clock from its resulting current bank. If removing those credits would leave either side without positive time, reject Undo without changing the position or clocks and explain the reason. This prevents repeated takebacks from manufacturing increment time. Reconcile an already expired clock first; Undo cannot erase a time result.

Invalidate in-flight requests and advance live request/position versions even when the board returns to an earlier FEN. Late replies from the discarded line cannot apply moves, consume attempts, add increment, or replace a result. Persist/sync the new current line so a stale tab or device cannot resurrect the discarded continuation.

An already recorded final result remains final. Undo applies only to an unfinished game or unfinished practice segment; Undo in practice never changes the original result. Playing an earlier position after a finalized game uses a separate custom-position game.

### Saving, accounts, and recovery

Guest play requires no account. Automatically save the full game in the same browser so refresh, navigation, and reopening can recover it. Browser data deletion/eviction can remove guest saves; show save failures rather than claiming a game is durably saved when it is not.

Optional accounts add cross-device game access and automatic synchronization for account-associated games. Keep a local copy for interrupted connectivity and sync pending changes when possible. Offer to add existing guest games to the signed-in account rather than silently merging unrelated games. Preserve identities, results, and current-line/archived-line distinctions during import. Signing in, signing out, syncing, and importing do not pause clocks or reset time. Private account games are accessible only to their owner.

Save the initial position, current rules state, accepted move history and repetition history, time control and clock references, model attributions and current/queued selections, request/position versions, spent turn budgets, complete retained conversation, separate received-data archive, final result/reason, and any practice segment. FEN alone cannot resume this contract. Account games remain available until their owner deletes them under the eventual data policy; implementation and storage limits must be addressed in architecture rather than silently dropping conversation history.

Support one authoritative writer per game across tabs/devices. Handoff or recovery must fence the earlier writer and its responses, preserve the live deadlines, and reject stale overwrites. An offline account copy cannot silently replace a newer accepted line or final result. The architecture must define the concrete ownership and conflict mechanism.

Reopening restores the game and reconciles elapsed time before play. Do not blindly repeat an in-flight request after refresh or handoff. Establish whether it is still actionable, fence it if abandoned, and offer explicit Retry or a model switch at the unchanged position when needed. The clock continues throughout this recovery. Any unfinished, unexpired game can continue with the same model or a newly selected model under the ordinary full-retained-history rule.

Proxy endpoints, credentials, storage/retention, and cross-device connection setup remain governed by [Choose supported proxy setups and credential handling](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-8/choose-supported-proxy-setups-and-credential-handling). Account sync is not permission to store proxy keys on the website's server. A second device may need its own supported route to the player's proxy.

### Endings and new games

Record win/loss/draw, side, and reason distinctly: checkmate, human resignation, model resignation, exhausted model illegal attempts, time loss, or the specific draw rule. A human may resign an unfinished game. Resolve any earlier authoritative clock expiry first. Starting another game, leaving, or disconnecting is not an implicit resignation or pause.

Preserve the agreed immediate model loss after an explicit refusal and the fourth illegal attempt. A technical error alone causes neither. A time loss is a separate reason. Results are final once recorded, and no stale response, retry, queued switch, Undo, or sync conflict may rewrite them.

New game/Restart opens setup and creates a separate game with fresh clocks and context after Start. The old game's history/result is preserved; an unfinished old game keeps its clock running unless it is explicitly resigned or otherwise ends. Do not implement Restart by erasing an existing match. Rematch also creates a new game, initially reusing the prior starting position, model, and time control with human colors swapped; allow setup changes before Start.

After a model loss on a still-playable board, offer the agreed explicit unscored practice continuation with the same or another model. Extend this to a model time loss as well as resignation/illegal-attempt loss. Preserve the original result and archive. Start a separate practice segment with fresh conversation and turn budgets, the actual retained rules/repetition state, and fresh clocks under the chosen time control. Its clocks begin only on Start practice and then obey the same continuous-time rules. Ordinary switches within practice carry that segment's full retained conversation. A practice ending never adds a new scored result to the original game.

A checkmated, stalemated, or otherwise terminal board cannot generate another move. Editing it starts a separate labeled custom-position game under the existing custom-start decision. That differs from unscored continuation of the unchanged playable board after a model loss.

### Required downstream verification

[Validate the connection and chess match interface](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-12/validate-the-connection-and-chess-match-interface) must cover setup/color/promotion, both live clocks, time-control selection, recovery with the clock still running, Undo and its context boundary, guest saves/account access, expired saved games, rematch, and distinct final/practice states on desktop/mobile.

[Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) must verify continuous clock authority with all clients closed, elapsed-time recovery, one-writer handoff, account ownership/storage, full archive/current-line separation, and the selected library's exact draw/timeout-mating rules. It owns the authentication mechanism, timer/state placement, background-processing limits, and reliable storage design.

[Agree on MVP acceptance criteria and the specification handoff](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-14/agree-on-mvp-acceptance-criteria-and-the-specification-handoff) must require evidence for clock expiry during thinking/retries/errors/closed tabs, boundary races and late responses, fresh clock snapshots on every request, promotion under time, Undo without time refunds or increment farming, branch-safe context replay and sync, guest/account resumption, interrupted requests, final-result preservation, draw rules, and practice clocks. Verify imported counters and retained versus reset repetition history.

No production implementation, model requests, browser prototype, or live compatibility checks were performed to settle this ticket. These requirements must be verified on the eventual implementation. No additional decision ticket is needed for these lifecycle defaults; remaining connectivity, model-selection, interface, architecture, and final acceptance questions remain in their existing tickets.

## Resolution

### Custom starting positions

The MVP will let human players set their own starting positions for play against a model opponent. Chess.com and Lichess were cited as familiar examples.

### Input methods

Support both a visual board editor where players arrange pieces and FEN import by pasting a position string.

### Position validation

Allow free editing of the setup, but block starting play until the position passes basic chess-validity checks. Invalid setups, such as a missing king or adjacent kings, must be corrected before play begins.

Check the current board and position settings for consistency. Do not require proof of a complete legal move history from the normal starting position.

Basic validation covers the input structure and field values, king placement, pawn ranks, side-to-move/check consistency, and declared castling/en passant state. Rejections must identify the failed check and affected setting or square so the player can correct it.

This is setup validation. It does not supply legal moves or strategic advice to the model.

### Position settings

The visual editor includes controls for the side to move, castling rights, and en passant state. Populate these settings automatically from imported FEN.

These settings are part of the starting position and must agree with the position used for play and supplied to the model.

### Custom-start results

A game started from a custom position records its own win, loss, or draw result and is labeled "Custom position."

Post-loss practice continuation remains unscored under the accepted decisions in [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

### Editing a position from an existing game

Starting play from an edited position creates a separate custom-position game. Preserve the original game and any recorded result.

The new game follows the custom-start result policy above and starts with fresh model context as specified below.

### Starting model context

A new custom-position game starts with fresh model context containing the usual game instructions, the starting FEN, and the readable piece list. Leave any source game's conversation with that original game.

This fresh start applies to new custom-position games. Ordinary mid-game model switches still carry that game's full prior conversation under [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

### Move counters and repetition history

Preserve the imported FEN's move number and fifty-move-rule counter. Count repeated positions only from the new custom-position game's start.

Do not invent earlier position history or carry the source game's repetition record into the separate custom-position game. These game-state rules are distinct from the fresh model conversation.

### Terminal starting positions

Allow checkmate and stalemate positions to remain viewable and editable. Disable Start game and clearly explain that the position is already terminal.

### Verification and downstream work

This resolves the product choices for custom starting positions. It does not claim that a chess library or prototype has passed these checks.

[Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) must verify the chosen chess library's current-position validation, FEN state preservation, and terminal-position detection against this boundary.

[Validate the connection and chess match interface](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-12/validate-the-connection-and-chess-match-interface) covers the editor, FEN import, actionable errors, and disabled Start game state. [Agree on MVP acceptance criteria and the specification handoff](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-14/agree-on-mvp-acceptance-criteria-and-the-specification-handoff) must include these scenarios and distinguish source facts from observed behavior.

Draw adjudication and resumption of existing games remain in [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle).

## Resolution

The cited report "Chess rules, board accessibility, and dependency licenses" and its reproducible evidence bundle are attached. Research source `47b57a492f61c5675301fb3e4dd33fa4d79930de` was integrated as `27a53c1`, at `research/chess-dependencies.md` and `experiments/chess-dependencies/`.

Attachment `d6c8fe58-5781-4da3-b737-3a765a7a2486` is the report, SHA-256 `d459fa7c88eb2b9a2031fee71eadf82e29450d57861eabb997b9175a75874050`, 49,752 bytes. Attachment `b838d3c8-6f96-4c70-80ea-1ea6aca0f6c5` is the 27-file evidence bundle, SHA-256 `fffdbf6b659dc26cc0cf9193f38abcfea9f1cf52e489537d5fd51a3ed97fd464`, 85,641 bytes. Both downloads were verified against their uploaded bytes.

### Rules findings

Neither chess.js 1.4.0 nor chessops 0.15.1 meets the full accepted contract alone. Both support useful legal-move, checkmate, and stalemate operations in the selected fixtures. The application must own strict orthodox FEN/current-state validation, exact counter and declared-right preservation, specific rule explanations, repetition history, adjudication order, Undo, clocks, and response fencing.

The probes reproduced unsafe acceptance or normalization of some invalid FEN settings. chess.js repetition misses the third occurrence in the sampled custom starts with ineffective imported en-passant metadata. At halfmove 100, checkmate and its fifty-move draw predicate can both be true, so the controller must give checkmate precedence. These are bounded observed cases, not a claim that ordinary legality universally fails.

A complete exploration of a locked-pawn-wall fixture reached 768 states and 3,808 legal transitions with no check, mate, pawn move, or disagreement between libraries. Both libraries' material helpers still failed to identify the dead position. An asymmetric wall fixture also distinguishes global deadness from one side's inability to mate.

CHA-Solver 3.0.0 is an MIT-licensed candidate for further investigation. Eight native Windows queries produced four unwinnable verdicts and four cooperative mating witnesses, replayed in both JS libraries. Its source includes an explicit unknown result and search limits. No browser/WASM build, general completeness proof, or mobile resource bound was established. This research does not resolve exact adjudication for every allowed custom position.

### Board and licenses

cm-chessboard has relevant keyboard/form, readable-board, and explicit promotion/focus mechanisms; gchessboard is another credible accessible starting point. react-chessboard and Chessground require more application-owned complete screen-reader interaction. None passed native browser or assistive-technology acceptance in this research. Preserve the approved Classic workspace.

chess.js is BSD-2-Clause; cm-chessboard and several other candidates are MIT. chessops and Chessground require GPL-compatible distribution of a combined covered frontend. Piece/marker art has separate terms, including CC BY-SA and optional NonCommercial assets. Preserve actual shipped notices and avoid presenting the complete dependency/art bundle as MIT-only. The owner has since delegated the project's license default to architecture; no new license preference question is needed.

### Verification and remaining work

The coordinator reran the JS probe in an ignored evidence cache. All 12 grouped assertions passed, including the 768-state closure, and the complete resulting JSON exactly matched the recorded evidence. All 26 normalized checksums, 62 report reference definitions, and local linked files checked. The researcher also recorded eight native solver queries and four legal mating-witness replays; those native queries were not rerun by the coordinator. Research working tree remained clean.

The architecture ticket must resolve the exact-adjudication gap or obtain an explicit owner amendment. A question is now pending there about accepting documented rare exceptions versus retaining exact rules and researching a specialized solver. Neither option is presumed approved.

No production implementation, browser/AT acceptance, provider calls, credentials, paid usage, service provisioning, push, or running helper was created. This ticket resolves the factual investigation and leaves the product decision in [Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries).

## Confirmed exact-adjudication requirement

The owner selected "Keep exact rules; research solver" on 2026-10-16. The proposed material-based MVP exceptions were not accepted.

Preserve complete dead-position detection and the position-sensitive timeout rule from [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle), including valid custom starting positions. Do not infer mating possibility from an unknown solver result, a fast helper returning false, lack of a found mate, or ordinary optimal-play tablebase WDL. Do not settle a provisional win and rewrite it later.

Continue with focused research into a browser-local specialized solver. Verify actual browser/WASM portability and bounded resource behavior separately from the source-level soundness, coverage, input assumptions, and undecided-result path. A successful sample is not evidence of complete coverage. The browser remains responsible for rules, clocks and match results; no hosted chess adjudication or AI generation relay is authorized.

No new question is pending. Existing free-tier, delegated-license and unsynced-local-continuation choices remain settled. Architecture stays In Progress until the evidence supports a concrete exact-adjudication design or exposes a precise remaining constraint for the owner.
